summary: NASA is exploring potential commercial servicing options for the Hubble Space Telescope, opening possibilities for private-sector maintenance of flagship civil space assets. In commercial aerospace, Virgin Galactic flew its new Delta-class space plane for the first time, while satellite operator Telesat faces an approaching C$2.4 billion debt maturity in December. Operational launch and orbital activity saw SpaceX deploy 27 Starlink satellites from California, India launch a next-generation navigation satellite, and observers track China’s mysterious space plane overhead in orbit. On defense and international fronts, Europe initiated funding for offensive in-space capabilities, the UK introduced local-investment rules for major foreign defense deals, and the Pentagon disclosed a $30.9 billion FY26 intelligence budget alongside plans to eye public-private partnerships for its FORTRESS America homeland base initiative. Within military personnel developments, promotions for the U.S. Space Force's second-highest enlisted rank expanded sharply. Deep-space scientific operations continued as NASA’s Voyager 1 resolved a brief communications pause through power-conservation measures, and the James Webb Space Telescope imaged the Cat’s Head Nebula while detecting a distant galaxy releasing ionizing radiation. Additionally, researchers demonstrated a new gel fuel to simplify rocket and satellite propulsion control, as well as photonic chips designed to link radio telescopes for higher-resolution imaging. Looking ahead, industry watchers are monitoring preparations for NASA’s newly scheduled launch of a next-generation ultraviolet space telescope in 2031.
